# Read in csv files
![](/images/csv_file.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}

There are various <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u> to __read__ in files into R. 
My favourite is `read.csv()`.
By default it will **read** in <u id='csv'>**csv**</u> files.  

## read.csv()

Use `read.csv()` to __read__ in the <u id='csv'>**csv**</u> file "Liverpool_beaches.csv".
```{r eval=FALSE}
liv_beaches_df <- read.csv("Liverpool_beaches.csv")
```

Have a look at the newly created <u id='data_frame_tooltip'>__data frame__</u>. 
Is it how you would like it?

## row.names = 1

The row names are empty and the beach names are in the first column. 
We'll fix this so the beach names are the row names. 
This can be carried out by including the option `row.names = 1` to specify that the 1st column will be read in as the row names.
```{r eval=FALSE}
liv_beaches_df <- read.csv("Liverpool_beaches.csv", row.names = 1)
```

We now know how to __read__ in a  <u id='csv'>**csv**</u> file with `read.csv`.
